title: Friday in the park
intro: On Fridays, the Iranian weekend, Tehran's parks fill up with families sitting on rugs under the trees. Reza, Mina and Sara go for a picnic too – but someone has forgotten the most important thing. The story practises the plural present (می‌روند، بازی می‌کنند), food and family words and the polite بفرمایید, and shows how a picnic in Iran can turn into a party.
source: An original story for this course.

sentences.fa: امروز جمعه است و هوا خوب است.
sentences.r: emruz jom'e ast o havā khub ast.
sentences.en: Today is Friday and the weather is good.

sentences.fa: رضا، مینا و سارا به پارک می‌روند.
sentences.r: Rezā, Minā o Sārā be pārk mi-ravand.
sentences.en: Reza, Mina and Sara go to the park.

sentences.fa: آن‌ها زیر یک درخت بزرگ می‌نشینند.
sentences.r: ān-hā zir-e yek derakht-e bozorg mi-neshinand.
sentences.en: They sit under a big tree.

sentences.fa: سارا و رضا فوتبال بازی می‌کنند.
sentences.r: Sārā o Rezā futbāl bāzi mi-konand.

sentences.en: Mina asks: "Reza, where is the tea flask?"

sentences.fa: رضا می‌گوید: «ای وای! فلاسک در خانه است!»
sentences.r: Rezā mi-guyad: «ey vāy! felāsk dar khāne ast!»
sentences.en: Reza says: "Oh no! The flask is at home!"

sentences.fa: کنار آن‌ها یک خانواده‌ی دیگر هست.
sentences.r: kenār-e ān-hā yek khānevāde-ye digar hast.
sentences.en: Next to them there is another family.

sentences.fa: مادر آن خانواده با یک سینی چای می‌آید.
sentences.r: mādar-e ān khānevāde bā yek sini chāy mi-āyad.
sentences.en: The mother of that family comes over with a tray of tea.
She says: "Please, have some fresh tea!"

sentences.fa: مینا هم به آن‌ها کوکو می‌دهد.
sentences.r: Minā ham be ān-hā kuku mi-dahad.
sentences.en: Mina gives them some kuku too.

sentences.fa: حالا دو خانواده با هم غذا می‌خورند.
sentences.r: hālā do khānevāde bā ham ghazā mi-khorand.
sentences.en: Now the two families eat together.

sentences.fa: سارا هم یک دوست جدید دارد.
sentences.r: Sārā ham yek dust-e jadid dārad.
sentences.en: And Sara has a new friend too.

vocab.en: kuku (a thick herb or potato omelette)
please (have some, come in, sit down)

after: Friday is the weekly holiday in Iran, and a picnic in the park – on a rug, with a flask of tea, bread and کوکو (a thick omelette full of herbs or potato) – is one of the great Iranian pleasures. Offering food to the people sitting next to you is perfectly normal, and so is giving something back: that is why Mina offers her kuku. بفرمایید is the all-purpose polite word for 'please, help yourself / come in / sit down / here you are'. ای وای! 'oh no!' is what you say when you realise you have forgotten something. And notice how دیگر after a noun with the ezafe means 'other': یک خانواده‌ی دیگر 'another family'.
